claims.text: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.

quotes.text: Hold a pair of dumbbells at your sides.
quotes.where: How to Do Dumbbell Shrugs, step 1

claims.text: Lift the shoulders straight up as high as possible, then lower them.

quotes.text: Lift your shoulders straight up as high as possible.
quotes.where: How to Do Dumbbell Shrugs, step 2

quotes.text: Lower your shoulders again.
quotes.where: How to Do Dumbbell Shrugs, step 3

claims.text: The shoulders do the lifting, not the arms or wrists; the arms stay straight while the shoulders rise toward the ears.

quotes.text: The movement should come from your shoulders, not your arms or wrists. Your arms should remain straight while you lift your shoulders up towards your ears.

claims.text: Stand with good posture and a braced trunk for the whole set.

quotes.text: Stand with the dumbbells in your hands, and make sure to keep a good posture and tension in your core during the entire movement.

claims.text: The range is short, so move slowly with a short pause at the top.

quotes.text: The range of motion in this exercise is quite short, so do the movement slow and controlled, preferably with a short pause in the top position to get a longer time under tension.

claims.text: A common mistake: arms not straight and passive, or shoulders moving forward or back instead of straight up and down.

quotes.text: Your arms should be straight and passive; the lifting motion should come entirely from your shoulders and traps. The shoulders should go straight up and down and not move forward/backward.
quotes.where: Common Mistakes: Not maintaining correct form

claims.text: Too heavy a weight makes good form hard to keep.

quotes.text: This is an exercise where it’s easy to pick both a weight that’s too heavy, which can lead to difficulties with keeping a proper form, and a weight that is too light.
quotes.where: Common Mistakes: Picking the wrong weight

claims.text: Lifting straps are fine when the grip limits the load.

quotes.text: If you feel like the grip strength is what’s holding you back from picking a heavier weight, don’t hesitate to use lifting straps.
quotes.where: Common Mistakes: Picking the wrong weight

claims.text: The dumbbell shrug works the upper trapezius, and the grip muscles too when no straps are used.

quotes.text: The dumbbel shrug works your upper trapezius muscle. If you are not using lifting straps to hold on to the dumbbells, you will also work your grip muscles.
quotes.where: Which Muscles Does Dumbbell Shrugs Work?

claims.text: The dumbbell version allows a slightly longer range than the barbell shrug.

quotes.text: The dumbbell version allows for a slighter longer range of motion, while most lifters find it easier to lift heavier in the barbell version.

claims.text: Tempo: about 1-2 s up and 1-2 s down, with a short pause at the top.

quotes.text: using 3- to 5-min rest periods between sets performed at a moderate contraction velocity (1-2 s CON; 1-2 s ECC).
preferably with a short pause in the top position

claims.text: Only raise and lower the shoulders; do not roll them (ACE barbell shrug page; same shoulder movement with dumbbells).

quotes.text: focus on only raising/lowering the shoulders - DO NOT roll the shoulders.

claims.text: Wrap the thumbs around the handle or bar.

quotes.text: Perform all grips with your thumbs around the bar.

claims.text: Grip is strongest with the wrist in its natural extended (bent-back) position, about 35 degrees, and weakens when the wrist moves away from it, even to 15 degrees of extension (measured on grip, applied here as a wrist cue).

quotes.text: Grip strength is significantly reduced when wrist position deviates from this self-selected optimum position.
The self-selected position was 35 degrees of extension and 7 degrees of ulnar deviation.
With the wrist in only 15 degrees of extension or in neutral radio-ulnar deviation, grip strength was reduced to two thirds to three fourths of normal.

claims.text: Add load in small steps (2-10%) only once the target reps are exceeded by one or two.

quotes.text: When training at a specific RM load, it is recommended that 2-10% increase in load be applied when the individual can perform the current workload for one to two repetitions over the desired number.

claims.text: Heavy lifting with a held breath (Valsalva) drives blood pressure very high.

quotes.text: It was concluded that when healthy young subjects perform weight-lifting exercises the mechanical compression of blood vessels combines with a potent pressor response and a Valsalva response to produce extreme elevations in blood pressure.

claims.text: The shoulder is one of the most common injury sites in resistance training (up to 36% of documented injuries), and poor technique is a named risk factor.

quotes.text: The results of the review indicated that up to 36% of documented RT-related injuries and disorders occur at the shoulder complex.
extrinsic risk factors, namely, that of improper attention to exercise technique.

claims.text: In EMG studies the shrug gives very high upper-trapezius activity: the one-arm shrug was the highest of ten exercises in healthy adults, and the shrug the highest of five in women with neck muscle pain (implement not stated in either abstract).

quotes.text: The unilateral shoulder shrug exercise was found to produce the greatest EMG activity in the upper trapezius.
For the trapezius muscle, the highest level of muscle activation was found during the shrug (102+/-11% of MVC), lateral raise (97+/-6% of MVC), and upright row (85+/-5% of MVC) exercises

plate.viewWhy: With a dumbbell at each side the weights hide behind the thighs side-on; front-on shows both shoulders rising level toward the ears and both arms staying straight (c1, c3). The census draws it front.
plate.equipment: Two dumbbells hanging at the sides from straight arms; floor line (c1).
plate.start: Standing tall, trunk braced (c4), arms straight at the sides holding the dumbbells, shoulders relaxed down (c1, c3).
plate.end: Same body; both shoulders lifted straight up toward the ears (c2, c3), arms still straight (c3).

checkpoints.label: Straight arms
checkpoints.what: Arms hang straight and passive; the shoulders do the lifting.

checkpoints.label: Straight up
checkpoints.what: Shoulders go straight up and down, not forward or back.

checkpoints.label: Stand tall
checkpoints.what: Good posture, trunk braced the whole set.

mistake.what: Elbows bend to pull the dumbbells up instead of the shoulders lifting them.
mistake.why: Rolling the shoulders (c12, from the barbell shrug page) is a rotation the engine cannot draw; bent, working arms are a named common mistake (c6) and show front-on as the dumbbells rise with the forearms.

grip.type: One dumbbell in each hand at the sides. No source read states the palm direction, so the sheet makes no palm claim.
grip.handContact: Handle across the middle of the palm, fingers wrapped (hold archetype); straps allowed when the grip limits the load.
grip.wrist: Bent back into its natural grip position (about 35 degrees), not curled forward; grip weakens when the wrist moves away from it.

setup.step: Pick up a dumbbell in each hand, thumbs around the handles.
Stand tall with the dumbbells at your sides.
Brace your trunk; arms straight and relaxed.

posture.point: Arms straight; the shoulders do the lifting.
Straight up and down, no rolling.
Short pause at the top, then lower slowly.

handlingMistakes.mistake: Bending the arms to pull the dumbbells up.
handlingMistakes.fix: Keep the arms straight and passive.

handlingMistakes.mistake: Rolling the shoulders or moving them forward and back.
Going too heavy to keep good form.
handlingMistakes.fix: Use lighter dumbbells, or straps if the grip is the limit.

rows.where: Top of the shoulders, between neck and shoulder
rows.means: Usually means the upper traps are lifting.
Usually means the grip is limiting the set.

rows.where: Sharp pain in the shoulder joint
rows.means: The shoulder is a common injury site in weight training; poor technique adds risk.

risks.risk: Holding your breath hard on heavy reps sends blood pressure very high.
The shoulder is a common injury site in weight training; poor technique adds risk.

zooms.right: Wrist bent back, in its natural grip position.
Both shoulders up toward the ears, arms straight.
zooms.wrong: Elbows bent, pulling the dumbbells up with the arms.
